assumptions: Fuel-cycle water only (crude production, crude transport, refining, distribution to pump).
Vehicle manufacture, maintenance, and road/rail/airport infrastructure are excluded.
Activity coefficient is a USLCI FY2025 Q2 technosphere exchange; USLCI water exchanges are deliberately not used (see uslci_audit.json).
Freshwater consumption, not withdrawal.

reference is passenger-km; occupancy already embedded — do NOT divide by occupancy again

water_intensity.basis: Central value is the midpoint of the well-to-pump consumptive range reported by Wu et al. (2009) for U.S. petroleum gasoline (2.8-6.6 L/L). The range is widened downward to 0.4 L/L to cover studies that count refining plus primary extraction only (King & Webber 2008, corroborated by the refinery unit processes in Grubert & Sanders 2018).
water_intensity.citation: Wu, M., Mintz, M., Wang, M. and Arora, S. (2009). "Water Consumption in the Production of Ethanol and Petroleum Gasoline." Environmental Management 44(5): 981-997. doi:10.1007/s00267-009-9370-0 (Argonne National Laboratory ANL/ESD/09-1, the water analysis that underpins the GREET water module.)
supporting_citations: King, C.W. and Webber, M.E. (2008). "Water Intensity of Transportation." Environmental Science & Technology 42(21): 7866-7872. doi:10.1021/es800367m

Grubert, E. and Sanders, K.T. (2018). "Water Use in the United States Energy System: A National Assessment and Unit Process Inventory of Water Consumption and Withdrawals." Environmental Science & Technology 52(11): 6695-6703. doi:10.1021/acs.est.8b00139

transport_factors.system_boundary: Fuel cycle only: crude production/recovery, crude transport, refining, and distribution to the pump (well-to-pump). Excludes vehicle manufacture, vehicle maintenance, road/rail/airport infrastructure, and end-of-life.

assumptions: Fuel-cycle water only (crude production, crude transport, refining, distribution to pump).
Vehicle manufacture, maintenance, and road/rail/airport infrastructure are excluded.
Activity coefficient is a USLCI FY2025 Q2 technosphere exchange; USLCI water exchanges are deliberately not used (see uslci_audit.json).
Freshwater consumption, not withdrawal.
Fuel water intensity is a U.S. literature constant (4.4 l water/l fuel, range 0.35-6.2); the range is wide because crude recovery method dominates.
reference is passenger-km; occupancy already embedded — do NOT divide by occupancy again

USLCI reports the identical fuel volume per p*km for the diesel and gasoline passenger car (0.0630015993522655 l). Treat the diesel car coefficient as a gasoline-derived placeholder, not an independent measurement.

activity.dataset_release: USLCI FY2025 Q2 (uslci_fy25_q2_01_json_ld.zip), Federal LCA Commons, National Renewable Energy Laboratory

water_intensity.basis: Diesel and gasoline share the same crude-production water burden, which is the dominant term, so diesel tracks gasoline closely. Set ~6% below gasoline because distillate requires less hydro-processing and reforming per litre than finished gasoline, and the refinery step is the part of the chain where the two fuels genuinely differ (Wu et al. 2009 refinery breakdown; Grubert & Sanders 2018 refinery unit processes). The range is scaled from the gasoline range on the same reasoning.
water_intensity.citation: Wu, M., Mintz, M., Wang, M. and Arora, S. (2009). "Water Consumption in the Production of Ethanol and Petroleum Gasoline."
